claims.text: Across 8 sensors and 3 production lines over 3 months, vibration levels and alarm rates are the primary signals to watch, with sensors S04–S06 running notably higher than the rest.
The dataset covers 17,630 readings from August through October 2026, capturing temperature, vibration, and alarm events across 3 lines and 8 sensors.
Vibration and alarms move together, and a cluster of sensors stands apart on vibration — both patterns deserve closer attention.
Sensors S04, S05, and S06 average vibration readings of 3.15, 3.21, and 3.19 mm/s respectively, while the remaining five sensors all average between 1.97 and 2.01 mm/s.
High vibration causes the alarms, so damping the line B sensors will stop them.
Temperature averages 92.4 across the three lines, with Line C the hottest by a wide margin.
264 alarms were recorded across 17,630 readings; the median reading carries no alarm, and the maximum is 1.00, confirming alarms are binary events.
Sensors S04, S05 and S06 are out of spec and the parts they monitor are defective. Addresses the clearest anomaly in the dataset before it escalates to alarms or downtime.

Review the 264 alarm events alongside their corresponding vibration readings to determine whether a vibration threshold reliably predicts alarms. Could enable earlier alarm intervention if a consistent vibration level precedes alarm events.
